title: Policy-led batchcache orchestration with forensic change control and RBAC workflows
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Overview:
We need an automated recommendation & safe-apply subsystem for batching and KV-prefix caching configurations that balances cost savings with strict compliance controls. This ticket scopes the engineering design and implementation for a policy-driven apply/rollback flow that produces immutable forensic audit records, enforces least-privilege RBAC and approval workflows, and supports deterministic rollback tokens for on-call recovery.

Problem statement:
- Recommendations (batch size, cache TTL, cache scope) can materially reduce inference costs but changing runtime configs automatically is a compliance risk.
- Current change path is manual: slow, error-prone, and hard to prove for auditors.
- We must enable safe automated application of changes for low-risk recommendations while ensuring high-risk changes require approvals and produce auditable evidence.

Goals:
- Build a policy evaluation engine that classifies recommendation risk (safe | review-required | blocked) using quant thresholds and historical impact models.
- Provide a secure auto-apply path for low-risk recommendations with signed change tokens and immutable audit events.
- Implement an approval workflow integrated with SSO/SCIM groups and our RBAC system for review-required changes.
- Record a complete forensic trace per change: who/what triggered it, input recommendation snapshot, modelled cost delta, before/after runtime config, rollout events, canary metrics, and final outcome.
- Support deterministic rollback using signed rollback tokens and automated verification of successful restoration.

Non-goals:
- This ticket does not change kernel selection or runtime batching internals; it focuses on config delivery, policy, security, and audit.

Design summary:
- Policy engine: rules expressed as a JSON policy language (authoring UX in Console later). Each rule returns a risk label and an allowed-apply window (time-to-live).
- Apply workflow: for low-risk changes the system mints a signed change token (ed25519) containing the change diff and policy decision. The token is pushed to the runtime via an authenticated service endpoint and accepted only if signature/nonce/timestamp check out.
- Approval workflow: review-required changes create an approval ticket in Console with reviewers derived from SSO groups. Approvals attach an approval token signed by the approver's SSO identity. The apply service requires either a change token (low-risk) or approval token + change token (high-risk) to proceed.
- Forensic audit: every state transition (recommend -> queued -> applied -> canary -> promote/rollback) emits an immutable audit record to the audit store (append-only topic with server-side encryption and KMS). Audit records include trace_id, change_token, approver_id, affected_customers (if any), metrics snapshot, and storage pointer to the recommendation payload.
- Rollback: when a rollback is requested (manual or automatic), the system uses the original change_token to compute a deterministic reverse diff and issues a signed rollback token. Rollbacks are recorded as first-class audit events and cross-checked by the runtime to avoid drift.

Compliance & retention:
- Audit retention: default 7 years for enterprise customers with SOC2/PCI options; compressed/archived storage after 1 year.
- Tamper-evidence: store hash chain (SHA-256) of consecutive audit records and persist chain anchors to object store and customer-managed KMS for Private installs.
- Access controls: only users with the audit_read role can export raw audit streams. Export actions are themselves audited.

Security considerations:
- Token signing keys are stored in KMS with key rotation policy.
- Apply endpoint enforces mTLS and checks service identity via SPIFFE.
- Rate-limit auto-applies and require human approval if failure/retry threshold exceeded.

Implementation plan (epics):
1) Policy evaluator + risk classification (service + unit tests)
2) Token format, signing, and apply endpoint (integration with KMS + runtime)
3) Approval UI + SSO group mappings + Console integration
4) Audit pipeline (append-only topic, retention, hash chaining)
5) Rollback orchestration and automated validation
6) Canary automation + alerts for regressions
7) Docs, runbook, and SOC-ready evidence pack

Rollout constraints:
- Private customers require ability to opt-out of auto-apply and keep recommendations only.
- Default enterprise config: auto-apply enabled for low-risk only; review-required default true for changes with modeled >5% cost delta or changes hitting >2 tenants.

Acceptance criteria:
- Policy engine classifies synthetic recommendation set with >=95% stability across runs.
- Low-risk changes can be auto-applied end-to-end in staging with signed tokens and produce audit records.
- Review-required flow triggers Console approvals, and approver signature is required for apply.
- Rollback from a canary failure completes and runtime returns to the previous stable config within SLA.
- Audit export contains chain anchors and enough metadata for an external auditor to reconstruct the change timeline.
acceptance_criteria: Policy evaluator deployed and unit-tested in staging
Auto-apply flow completes with signed change tokens and immutable audit records
Approval flow requires SSO-signed approver token for high-risk changes
Deterministic rollback validated against canary failure scenarios
Audit exports reproduce change timeline with chain anchors
tasks: Design JSON policy schema and rule library
Integrate token signing with KMS and rotation
Add apply endpoint with mTLS and SPIFFE checks
Build Console approval UI and SSO group mapping
Create audit append-only topic and retention job
Implement rollback orchestration and validation tests
Create canary alerting and automated promote/rollback hooks
Write runbook and SOC2 evidence pack
rollout_plan: Deploy policy evaluator to staging behind feature flag
Run offline scoring on historical recommendations for calibration
Enable low-risk auto-apply in staging with short TTL tokens
Execute canary applies to subset of tenants and monitor cost/latency dashboards
Open limited production pilot with internal customers
Widen pilot if post-canal metrics within thresholds
Enable default enterprise settings after security review
audit_schema: Fields: trace_id, timestamp, actor_id (service|user), actor_identity_provider, change_token, rollback_token, policy_id, risk_label, change_diff_uri, before_config_uri, after_config_uri, canary_metrics_snapshot_uri, outcome, signed_by, signature_algorithm, sha256_chain_anchor. Retention: 7 years default, compressed archive after 1 year.
rbac_model: Roles: batch_reviewer (can view recommendations, comment), batch_applier (can auto-apply low-risk with service identity), approver (can approve high-risk changes), audit_reader (can read raw audit), admin (full). Controls: approval_required flag per policy, SSO group -> role mapping, least-privilege service identities for token minting.
telemetry_and_alerts: Emit metrics: recommendations_evaluated, recommendations_applied, recommendations_rejected, autoapply_failures, rollbacks_triggered, canary_regressions. Alerts: autoapply_failures >5 in 1h, canary_regressions exceed threshold, audit_write_failures. Dashboards: per-model/per-tenant cost delta, token issuance rate.
